text:
Lots of good discussion on systemic fixes, but if you're running WordPress today: do a plugin audit. Go through every plugin and check whether the developer is still active and whether ownership has changed — you can see this on the wordpress.org plugin page. Remove anything you're not actively using. A plugin you forgot about is exactly the kind of thing an attacker buys.

More broadly, the rules around plugin marketplaces were set up for a different time. There's no requirement to disclose ownership transfers, no mandatory code review after a sale, and no way for users to get notified when the person behind a plugin they trust is no longer the same person. The laws and platform policies need to catch up to the reality that plugin acquisitions are now a known attack vector.
